documents.title: OU Guidelines: Artificial Intelligence Usage
documents.stance_why: The document says "AI tools are permitted to support decision-making, research, and operational efficiency" with disclosure, but for teaching it only says "Please refer to AI Guidance provided by the ... (CETL)" and sets no academic-use stance, so it delegates.
documents.summary: A university IT standard on responsible AI use mainly for operations, data and decisions about people. It permits AI with disclosure and human oversight but sends teaching, learning and integrity to CETL and research to the Research Office.

units.why: The overview says "AI tools are permitted to support decision-making, research, and operational efficiency", a default allowance for the university's AI use, so P02 (permit by default) with actor all.
units.anchor: AI tools are permitted to support decision-making, research, and operational efficiency

units.why: "All AI use requires disclosure" is a blanket duty to disclose AI use, so P24; the 'rigorous review' part is not separately specified.
units.anchor: All AI use requires disclosure, rigorous review, and safeguard
units.policy: All AI use requires disclosure, rigorous review, and safeguards.
units.fit_note: Also requires rigorous review and safeguards, which P24 does not capture.

units.why: The sentence states the purpose and scope ("across Oakland University's academic, research, clinical, and business operations"), which is an institution-wide framework preamble, P56.
units.anchor: establish a framework for responsible, ethical, and strategic use of Generative Artificial Intelligence
units.policy: The guidelines establish a framework for responsible, ethical, and strategic use of GenAI and LLMs across academic, research, clinical, and business operations.

units.why: A guiding principle ('Academic Integrity') that sets the framework's values, not a specific rule, so P56 informs.
units.anchor: Preserving the fundamental values of intellectual honesty, original thought, and scholarly rigor

units.why: The 'Ethical Deployment' principle states values for the whole framework ("respect for human values, individual rights"), so P56.
units.anchor: implemented with a fundamental respect for human values, individual rights, and societal well-being

units.why: The 'Accessibility & Equity' principle asks that tools be "inclusive and accessible", nearest type is P51 (equity and access); P53 would fit the bias part but access is the lead idea.
units.anchor: Ensuring AI tools are inclusive and accessible, avoiding bias
units.fit_note: Also names avoiding bias and disproportionate impacts, which goes beyond access and cost.

units.why: "must include active human involvement and accountability" keeps humans responsible for decisions, matching P73.
units.anchor: All AI-assisted decision-making processes must include active human involvement and accountability.

units.why: Data going in and out of AI systems "must be handled according to" the Data Classification Standard, a data protection duty, P50.
units.anchor: must be handled according to the University’s Data Classification Standard

units.why: The clause continues the data-handling sentence and requires compliance with "external legal and regulatory frameworks", which is P77 (comply with law).
units.anchor: external legal and regulatory frameworks
units.policy: AI data handling must follow external legal and regulatory frameworks.

units.why: "must be safeguarded from unauthorized access, upload, and misuse" protects confidential data in AI use, P50.
units.anchor: Confidential \Internal data must be safeguarded from unauthorized access, upload, and misuse

units.why: Data entered into unauthorized AI is treated as an incident that "must follow" the CIRP steps, a reporting channel for data exposure, P71.
units.anchor: must follow the steps defined in Oakland University’s Cyber Incident Response Program
units.policy: Entering Confidential and Internal Data into unauthorized AI systems is a public disclosure and must follow the steps defined in the Cyber Incident Response Program.

units.why: "please confer with UTS first" is advice to check before putting confidential data in AI, a data protection step, P50 with modality should.
units.anchor: Note: If you intend on entering Confidential Data in an AI tool please confer with

units.why: Procurement "must verify vendor compliance" with privacy law for third-party AI, an institutional review of AI vendors, P65.
units.anchor: procurement must verify vendor compliance

units.why: "required to pause and verify the classification" before pasting data into AI protects confidential data, P50.
units.anchor: you are required to pause and verify the classification of that data

units.why: A factual warning that prompts are effectively public, supporting the data protection rule, P50 informs.
units.anchor: inputting data into these systems is equivalent to publishing it in a public forum

units.why: "will not be solely used to make personnel, award, or disciplinary decisions" bars AI as sole basis for decisions about people, P73.
units.anchor: GenAI and LLMs will not be solely used to make personnel, award, or disciplinary decisions.

units.why: "Decision-making may not be delegated to GenAI systems" keeps humans deciding, P73.
units.anchor: Decision-making may not be delegated to GenAI systems.

units.why: Describes institutional review of AI tools before adoption ("thorough evaluation by cross-functional experts"), P65.
units.anchor: all AI tools undergo thorough evaluation by cross-functional experts before implementation

units.why: Approved AI systems get "re-evaluation upon major updates", a continuing tool review; P65 (tool review) fits better than P54, which is about revisiting the policy.
units.anchor: All approved AI systems are subject to re-evaluation upon major updates or model changes.

units.why: Research use is handed to "AI In Research Guidance" from the Research Office, so the rule for research and scholarship lives elsewhere, P62.
units.anchor: AI In Research Guidance provided by The Research Office
units.fit_note: Only a pointer to the research guidance, no rule is stated.

units.why: Teaching, learning and academic integrity are handed to CETL guidance, so this document sets no academic stance itself and delegates the decision (P04).
units.anchor: AI Guidance provided by the Center for Excellence in Teaching and Learning (CETL)
units.fit_note: Delegates to a central teaching center's guidance rather than to instructors directly.

units.why: Finance and Administration may use AI for "institutional efficiency", an operational rule outside teaching, P76.
units.anchor: AI may be used for enhancing institutional efficiency

units.why: Finance recommendations from AI "must be reviewed and approved by appropriate human decision-makers", human review of AI-supported decisions, P73.
units.anchor: AI-generated recommendations must be reviewed and approved by appropriate human decision-makers.

units.why: Planning use of AI is allowed but "must not replace human judgment"; this is operational use, not a decision about individuals, so P76 rather than P73.
units.anchor: must not replace human judgment

units.why: "Ongoing performance monitoring is required" for AI in planning is an operational control, P76.
units.anchor: Ongoing performance monitoring is required to detect bias, errors, or deviations from institutional values.

units.why: AI may screen but "may not make personnel decisions", a consequential decision about people, P73.
units.anchor: may not make personnel decisions

units.why: "require human oversight" for HR uses keeps a human responsible for decisions about employees, P73.
units.anchor: All HR-related uses of AI require human oversight to prevent bias and protect employee rights.

units.why: Student Affairs may use AI for administrative functions, operational use outside teaching, P76.
units.anchor: AI may enhance administrative functions such as registrar processes

units.why: "prohibited from making independent enrollment or disciplinary decisions" about students, with human review required, P73.
units.anchor: AI is prohibited from making independent enrollment or disciplinary decisions

units.why: A governance body is created to "oversee policy implementation, review incidents"; it is institution-level framework structure, nearest P56.
units.anchor: will establish an AI Governance Council
units.fit_note: Creates an oversight council; P56 covers frameworks and principles, not named bodies.

units.why: "will be reviewed annually" sets a review cycle, P54.
units.anchor: These guidelines will be reviewed annually

units.why: A duty to report "misuse, unintended consequences, or ethical concerns" through a named channel, P71.
units.anchor: must be reported via the AI Incident Reporting Process

units.why: Violations fall under "applicable university policies" with unspecified action, so P77 (existing policy governs) rather than P37, which needs concrete penalties.
units.anchor: may result in disciplinary or administrative action

units.why: The Chief Information Security Officer holds "authority for interpretation, monitoring, and enforcement"; no type covers assigning policy ownership.
units.anchor: Primary authority for interpretation, monitoring, and enforcement of this standard
units.uncovered_note: Names which office owns interpretation, monitoring and enforcement of the AI guidelines.

documents.unit: Center for Excellence in Teaching and Learning (AI@OU)
documents.title: Students - AI@OU
documents.stance_why: Although students are "encouraged to explore" GenAI, the rule is "Always assume that the use of generative AI is prohibited unless your instructor explicitly allows it", so AI is banned unless permitted, which is restrict.
documents.summary: Student-facing AI@OU guidance: AI use must follow the Student Code of Conduct and be authorized by the course instructor, with a default that AI is prohibited unless allowed. It adds duties to cite, document, fact-check and protect data, and a good-practice versus poor-practice table.

units.why: Opening sentence says students "are encouraged to explore" GenAI tools, an encouragement, though qualified by instructor authorization in the next sentence.
units.anchor: students are encouraged to explore
units.fit_note: The encouragement is bounded by the instructor-authorization rule that follows.

units.why: "must adhere to the OU Student Code of Conduct" ties AI use to an existing policy, P77.
units.anchor: all use of GenAI must adhere to the OU Student Code of Conduct

units.why: AI use "must be explicitly authorized and defined by the individual course instructor", so the rule is set per instructor (P04); the implied default ban is coded separately as P06.
units.anchor: must be explicitly authorized and defined by the individual course instructor
units.policy: All use of GenAI must be explicitly authorized and defined by the individual course instructor.

units.why: "fact-check all output" is a duty to verify AI output, P31.
units.anchor: fact-check all output to maintain academic integrity

units.why: "cite and document every contribution made by an AI tool" is a disclosure duty, P24.
units.anchor: cite and document every contribution made by an AI tool

units.why: "exclusively using institutional AI tools for academic work" prefers vetted tools for privacy, P50.
units.anchor: exclusively using institutional AI tools for academic work
units.policy: Students must prioritize data privacy and security by exclusively using institutional AI tools for academic work.

units.why: "never inputting confidential or sensitive information into public-facing models" protects personal data, P50.
units.anchor: never inputting confidential or sensitive information into public-facing models

units.why: AI as "not a shortcut that compromises your development" is a rationale that shortcuts undercut skill building, P41.
units.anchor: not a shortcut that compromises your development of essential critical skills

units.why: The page points students to an external AI field guide with "mini-tools" to build AI literacy, P70.
units.anchor: a practical framework for navigating artificial intelligence responsibly
units.fit_note: Points to an external guide rather than offering or mandating training.

units.why: "Your individual instructor and the specific assignment determine the rules" puts the decision with instructor and assignment, P04.
units.anchor: Your individual instructor and the specific assignment determine the rules for using GenAI in your

units.why: A fallback when the syllabus is silent: "assume ... prohibited unless your instructor explicitly allows it"; P06 fits more exactly than P01 because the ban depends on instructor silence.
units.anchor: Always assume that the use of generative AI is prohibited unless your instructor explicitly allows

units.why: "talk to your instructor before you start" when unsure is the ask-first rule, P10.
units.anchor: talk to your instructor before you start

units.why: Notes courses may range from prohibited to "required" so the rule varies by course, P04.
units.anchor: prohibited in one course, permitted with acknowledgment in another and even required in a third

units.why: Rules can change "from one assignment to the next", per-assignment deciding, P04.
units.anchor: one course may allow varying levels of permitted GenAI from one assignment to the next

units.why: "rules for that specific course" says each course's policy governs only that course, P11.
units.anchor: Your compliance is based on the rules for that specific course

units.why: "transparency is required" when AI use is permitted, a general disclosure duty, P24.
units.anchor: transparency is required

units.why: The documentation list names the tool, "your original prompt" and what was done with the output, the specifics P25 covers.
units.anchor: What you asked it to do (your original prompt).
units.policy: Students must be prepared to document how they used the tool: the name of the tool, the original prompt, and what they did with the output.

units.why: "You must cite GenAI whenever you use its output" is a citation duty covering text, code and images, P24.
units.anchor: You must cite GenAI whenever you use its output in your work

units.why: "recommended practice to save all chat transcripts" and keep them for the instructor, P26 with modality should.
units.anchor: it is recommended practice to save all chat transcripts from GenAI tools

units.why: "accountable for everything you submit" is student ownership of submitted work, P29.
units.anchor: You are the author, and you are accountable for everything you submit.

units.why: "critically evaluate and verify" AI output against external sources, P31.
units.anchor: You must critically evaluate and verify all information, sources and data

units.why: States that models "perpetuate societal biases", a bias concern, P53.
units.anchor: can contain and perpetuate societal biases

units.why: "Review the output for ... biases" asks students to check AI output critically, P31.
units.anchor: Review the output for any harmful, unfair or inaccurate biases.

units.why: AI should "supplement your effort, not replace it", so students stay the primary worker, P32.
units.anchor: only when used to supplement your effort, not replace it

units.why: Explains why reliance is limited: it "can hinder your development" of skills, P41.
units.anchor: Over-reliance on GenAI can hinder your development of essential critical thinking

units.why: "Always check with your instructor first" even for the listed good practices is the ask-first rule, P10.
units.anchor: Always check with your instructor first before using a GenAI tool

units.why: Listed under brainstorming as 'Good Practice': generating ideas and outlining, P15.
units.anchor: Generate ideas, create project titles or outline a paper's structure.

units.why: Study-aid use listed as good practice: "practice quizzes or flashcards", P14.
units.anchor: Create practice quizzes or flashcards based on your notes or a reading.

units.why: Clarification use: asking AI to explain a concept, P12.
units.anchor: Ask for a difficult concept to be explained in simpler terms or a different analogy.

units.why: Practicing prompt design is building an AI skill, P44.
units.anchor: Experiment with prompts to improve the quality of the output

units.why: Listed under 'Poor Practice': submitting an AI-generated paper "as your own work", P19.
units.anchor: Submit an AI-generated essay, paper or lab report as your own work.

units.why: 'Poor Practice': AI summaries "instead of doing the reading yourself" skips the practice that builds skill, P41.
units.anchor: Rely on AI-generated summaries of course readings instead of doing the reading yourself.
units.fit_note: Stated as a discouraged practice, not only as rationale.

units.why: 'Poor Practice': having AI "solve homework problems or complete assignments", producing submitted work, P19.
units.anchor: Ask the GenAI to solve homework problems or complete assignments that are meant to build

units.why: 'Poor Practice': accepting output "without critical evaluation", P31.
units.anchor: Accept the first output a GenAI tool provides without critical evaluation or refinement.

units.why: The 'Core Principle' warns that offloading thought sacrifices skill development, P41.
units.anchor: you are sacrificing the opportunity to develop the skills that will be crucial

units.why: Explains why university-licensed tools are safer, supporting preference for vetted tools, P50.
units.anchor: Your data and chat history are private and not used to train the underlying AI

units.why: "Always use the institutional version for academic work" prefers vetted tools, P50.
units.anchor: Always use the institutional version for academic work

units.why: "DO NOT enter confidential, restricted or sensitive ... information" protects personal data, P50.
units.anchor: DO NOT enter confidential, restricted or sensitive University or personal information

units.why: Course materials, assignments and forum posts "should not be uploaded" without consent; P49 chosen over P20 because it centers on course materials and faculty consent.
units.anchor: should not be uploaded or input into a GenAI tool without faculty consent

units.why: Tells students AI is not authoritative, so output needs checking, P31.
units.anchor: predictive models, not authoritative knowledge bases

units.why: "treated with suspicion" tells students to verify output, P31.
units.anchor: Treat GenAI output as a first draft or a source to be treated with suspicion

units.why: Urges students to "develop your AI Literacy", an AI-literacy goal, P70.
units.anchor: Develop your AI Literacy to be a confident and ethical user
units.fit_note: An exhortation to self-study; no training is offered or required here.

units.why: Students are told to read each syllabus's integrity policy; P09 binds instructors and P11 is about non-carryover, so no type fits.
units.anchor: Review the academic integrity policy provided in each of your course syllabi.
units.uncovered_note: Students are told to read the academic integrity policy in each course syllabus.

units.why: "Experiment with different AI tools" encourages building AI skill, P44; it sits in tension with the instructor-first default.
units.anchor: Experiment with different AI tools to understand their unique strengths and weaknesses.

units.why: Advises AI for phases that do not assess core learning, e.g. "brainstorming, outlining, light editing"; P15 leads, with editing beyond it.
units.anchor: Use GenAI to enhance the phases of your work that don't directly assess your core
units.fit_note: Also covers outlining and light editing, and ties the permission to which phases assess core learning.

documents.unit: Center for Excellence in Teaching and Learning (AI@OU)
documents.title: Faculty - AI@OU
documents.stance_why: The document says "Faculty members have discretion to set policies for GenAI use in their courses" and offers tiered sample statements and a scale, so it sets no stance of its own and delegates, with tiers listed.
tiers: Limited Use (GenAI as a Learning Tool)
Integrated Use (GenAI as a Writing Assistant)
Encouraged Use with Critical Engagement (GenAI Literacy Focus)
documents.summary: CETL faculty guidance: faculty define GenAI boundaries per course or assignment, put them in the syllabus, treat unauthorized use as misconduct, and are warned off relying on detectors. It offers sample syllabus statements at four course levels and a five-level AI Assessment Scale.

units.why: The center "invites faculty to actively redefine academic integrity in their courses", leaving the rule to each instructor, P04.
units.anchor: invites faculty to actively redefine academic integrity in their courses

units.why: States the university's guiding aim ("supports, rather than supplants, critical thinking"), a framework principle, P56.
units.anchor: intentional AI integration that supports, rather than supplants, critical thinking

units.why: Requires adherence to "foundational ... UTS Policies", existing policy, P77.
units.anchor: adhering to foundational University Technology Services (UTS) Policies on data security

units.why: CETL is named the "primary resource" for faculty on AI, support for faculty learning, P63.
units.anchor: serves as the primary resource for the ethical and practical integration

units.why: "training, resources and consultative support" for faculty, P63.
units.anchor: we provide the training, resources and consultative support

units.why: The center balances students developing "their own understanding independent of AI" with adoption, a skill-building rationale, P41.
units.anchor: students to develop their own understanding independent of AI

units.why: A CETL resource guiding faculty to use AI in course design, faculty support, P63.
units.anchor: a practical guide for using generative AI to support thoughtful, student-centered course design

units.anchor: use it to create grading rubrics, format quiz questions to import

units.anchor: AI can support accessibility by helping make course content accessible

units.anchor: offers a network of specialized training and resource hubs across campus

units.why: Describes research-specific AI guidance across "the complete research lifecycle", P62.
units.anchor: provides specific guidance to assist investigators in navigating the ethical and responsible integration

units.why: The research framework has researchers "transparently document AI contributions", an AI rule in research, P62.

units.why: Introduces the Assessment-Level AI Integration Scale for choosing AI use per assignment, P05.
units.anchor: help faculty make intentional choices about when and how GenAI should be used in assignments

units.why: The 'No AI' level of the scale defines a named tier, P05.
units.anchor: The assessment is completed entirely without AI assistance in a controlled environment

units.why: Sample 'No AI' statement bans AI during the assessment, P22.
units.anchor: You must not use AI at any point during the assessment

units.why: The 'AI Planning' tier is a named level permitting pre-task use, P05.
units.anchor: AI may be used for pre-task activities such as brainstorming, outlining and initial research

units.why: Sample 'AI Planning' statement permits AI for planning and idea development, P15.
units.anchor: You may use AI for planning, idea development and research

units.why: The 'AI Collaboration' tier is a named level allowing drafting and feedback, P05.
units.anchor: AI may be used to help complete the task, including idea generation, drafting, feedback and

units.why: At the Collaboration level, students "should critically evaluate and modify" output, P31.
units.anchor: Students should critically evaluate and modify the AI-suggested outputs

units.why: Sample Collaboration statement permits AI "drafting text", prose use, P18.
units.anchor: You may use AI to assist with specific tasks such as drafting text, refining and

units.why: Sample statement requires evaluating AI content, P31.
units.anchor: You must critically evaluate and modify any AI-generated content you use

units.why: The 'Full AI' tier is a named level allowing AI on any element, P05.
units.anchor: AI may be used to complete any elements of the task

units.why: At the Full AI level assessments "may also require engagement with AI", AI expected in the work, nearest P02.
units.anchor: Assessments at this level may also require engagement with AI
units.fit_note: States a possible requirement to use AI, not only permission.

units.why: Sample Full AI statement: "You may use AI extensively", P02.
units.anchor: You may use AI extensively throughout your work

units.why: The 'AI Exploration' tier is a named level where AI is used creatively, P05.
units.anchor: AI is used creatively to enhance problem-solving, generate novel insights

units.why: At this level "students and educators co-design assessments", co-creation with students, P67.
units.anchor: Students and educators co-design assessments to explore unique AI applications
units.fit_note: Co-designs assessments rather than the course AI policy.

units.why: Sample Exploration statement: "You should use AI creatively", P02.
units.anchor: You should use AI creatively to solve the task

notes: Coder A. No school or computing-unit AI policy was collected; course layer deferred. Doc oakland-1 is a security/operations standard whose teaching content is only a pointer to CETL. Doc oakland-2 default (prohibited unless instructor allows) sits alongside an encouragement to explore; both coded. Doc oakland-3 sample syllabus statements and the AI Assessment Scale are coded as examples offered to faculty, not as university rules.
